exposure: fetal birth weight (<2,500g, ≥2,500g and <4,500g (normal), ≥4,000g and <4,250g, ≥4,250g and <4,500g, ≥4,500g)
cohort: 5,177 singleton pregnancies resulting in live births at or after 37 weeks gestation, delivered between January 1st 2006 and December 31st 2011 at a university hospital
finding: Fetal birth weight below 2,500g and above 4,250g was associated with some risks, but there was no general contraindication for attempting a vaginal delivery in a university hospital setting.
mod_finding: Second stage cesarean section was significantly more likely when fetal birth weight was under 2,500g compared to normal birth weight (odds ratio 3.01, 95% confidence interval 2.03-4.46, p value < 0.001).
